Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the fix (keeping the recurrence iterator index aligned with the timestamp) in the pkg/timeutil recurrence code. The raw summary and PR objectives both describe this exact change: restoring the iteration index when a candidate is rejected in IterateFromNextAfter and IterateFromPrevBefore. The title is concise, specific, and conventional.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#5521`] The issue asks for the backwards-loop paths in IterateFromNextAfter and IterateFromPrevBefore to keep iteration and At aligned. The diff at pkg/timeutil/recurrence.go adds `ic += 1` before the `break` in the future-anchor loop of iterateFromNextAfterInclusive (the `v.Before(t)` check). It adds `ic -= 1` before the `break` in the past-anchor loop of iterateFromPrevBeforeInclusive (the `v.After(t)` check). In both paths, res holds the instant for the restored index, so Next() and Prev() recompute the same instant the caller already holds. The other loop branches already update res and ic together, so they need no change. The issue's acceptance criterion for chained-iteration tests is addressed by the new TestRecurrenceIteratorNavigation in pkg/timeutil/recurrence_test.go, per the change summary. I did not read the test file hunks directly, so the test coverage verdict rests on the summary. No non-coding requirement applies.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The code change is two added lines in pkg/timeutil/recurrence.go, one per affected backwards-loop path. The test file adds a navigation test for monthly recurrences, which supports the linked issue. The PR description and the PR objectives both state that no grant-balance change is made. The diff contains no unrelated edits, so no out-of-scope changes were found.
